name: Chehalis
tax_rate: 2% (DOR Q2 2026 flyer; total lodging rate 10.4%) plus a $2.00 per room-night Tourism Promotion Area charge on lodging with 40 or more units (TPA code 2102)
deadline_pattern: Main round: applications released late July/August and due in early September (noon Sept 8, 2025 for 2026 funds; 4 p.m. Sept 6, 2024 after extension for 2025 funds). A second window has been opened in February to allocate funds left over from the main round (Feb 2024 for 2024 funds). 2027 deadline not confirmed; the city website could not be fetched.
typical_open: Late July to mid-August (press release July 28, 2025; Aug 14, 2024)
annual_pool: 2024 starting funds $570,744 (per council report), of which $71,819 went to Recreation Park debt service and $50,000 was held as reserve; $302,900 awarded in the October 2023 round and $146,719 left for a second 2024 round. 2026 allocations approved by council with a $50,000 reserve retained (citizenportal.ai headline; article not readable). 2027 pool not published.
contact: Chehalis City Manager's Office, 360-345-1042 ext. 203 (Jill Anderson, City Manager); no email published in press coverage
notes: Chehalis LTAC takes applications once a year in late summer for the next budget year, with the committee meeting in the fall and council approving awards in October; when money is left over the city has reopened applications in February for a spring round. The committee funds tax-exempt organizations and government entities only, and has pushed back on visitor-center operations and applicants without financial statements, favoring digital marketing and events with overnight-stay potential. The city website (ci.chehalis.wa.us) returned errors on every fetch, so 2026 and 2027 details come from Chronicle and Yahoo News coverage.

presentation.pattern: Not described in press coverage; LTAC met March 8, 2024 to score the spring-round applications about four weeks after they were received

meeting_schedule: Meets as needed: fall (September/October) to review main-round applications and in March when a spring round is opened; council acts on recommendations at a regular Monday meeting (Oct 2023, March 25, 2024)
pool_note: 2024 figures from The Chronicle: $570,744 starting LTAC funds minus $71,819 Recreation Park debt service and $50,000 reserve leaves $448,925 open to applicants ($302,900 awarded Oct 2023 plus $146,719 for the Feb 2024 round; the article's own subtraction is $694 off). 2025-2027 totals not published in readable sources.

tax_rate: 2% on lodging with 39 or fewer units and 3% on 40 or more units (DOR Q2 2026 flyer; total lodging rates 10.2% and 11.2%)
deadline_pattern: Fall cycle: applications accepted September 1-30 (5 p.m.) for the next budget year; spring cycle: March 1-31 for funds set aside for the current year. Kalama Tourism Advisory Committee reviews on the 2nd Wednesday of October and the 2nd Wednesday of April.

notes: Kalama runs its lodging tax through a seven-member Kalama Tourism Advisory Committee (KTAC) with two application windows a year, September for next-year funding and March for current-year funds, scored on a 100-point rubric (25 points tourism/overnight stays, 20 impact, 15 community support, 15 promotion, 10 capacity, 15 match). The packet admits public, nonprofit or private entities, so for-profits can apply directly. Pool size and committee names are not posted.
